steps.tx: **Pasteurisation** is targeted disinfection, not sterilisation: holder method 63 degrees for 30 minutes or flash (HTST) 72 degrees for 15 seconds kills milk's vegetative pathogens (Mycobacterium tuberculosis historically, Coxiella burnetii the benchmark, Salmonella, Brucella, Listeria, Campylobacter) while sparing flavour and leaving spores and thermoduric organisms alive, which is why pasteurised milk still refrigerates and still spoils.
steps.say: Pasteurisation kills milk's pathogens, not its spores; refrigeration finishes the job.

left.title: Methods
points: UHT: 135 C seconds, near sterilisation shelf stable

steps.tx: **Inspissation** solidifies egg and serum media by gentle heating (80 to 85 degrees for thirty minutes on successive days in an inspissator), the heat coagulating egg protein into Lowenstein Jensen slopes while disinfecting them; Loeffler serum slopes for diphtheria work share the technique. Fractional gentle heat here serves texture and sterility together, Tyndallisation's close cousin in the media kitchen.
steps.say: Inspissation cooks egg media just enough to set and disinfect, never to sterilise.

right.title: Media kitchen neighbours
points: Heat labile additives after cooling to 50 C (blood agar)
Chocolate agar: blood heated to release factors
Filter sterilised sugars and urea added aseptically

steps.tx: **Vaccine and serum** heat treatments borrow pasteurisation logic: water bath inactivation of complement in serum at 56 degrees for thirty minutes (serology's routine), heat killed vaccines historically, and blood product viral inactivation by pasteurisation and solvent detergent methods. Each is pathogen reduction tuned to preserve a fragile biological product, the same compromise milk taught.
steps.say: Fifty six degrees for thirty minutes inactivates complement; heat is dosed like a drug everywhere.

right.title: Verification tests
points: Methylene blue reductase keeps quality grade
Coliform counts audit post process contamination

steps.tx: Cold sterilisation by **filtration** handles what no heat survives: sera, antibiotic solutions, sugar media, and air (HEPA filters in laminar flows and theatres) pass through 0.22 micrometre membranes that retain bacteria while viruses and mycoplasma (0.1 to 0.3 micrometre filters respectively) challenge finer grades. Filter integrity (bubble point) testing certifies the invisible barrier.
steps.say: A 0.22 micrometre membrane sterilises fluids heat would ruin; viruses pass and must be handled otherwise.

left.title: Filtration territory
points: Heat labile fluids: sera, antibiotics, vitamins
0.22 um retains bacteria, 0.1 um targets mycoplasma
HEPA air in laminar flow and theatres
Viruses and prions not retained reliably

steps.tx: **Radiation sterilises at** factory scale: gamma from cobalt 60 (and electron beam) penetrates packaged syringes, gloves and sutures in sealed cartons, dosed in kilograys against spore benchmarks, while ultraviolet stays a surface and air adjunct (theatres, cabinets) because shadows and poor penetration betray it. Radiation leaves no residue but demands licensed facilities, dividing factory from hospital methods.
steps.say: Gamma sterilises sealed cartons by the pallet; UV only disinfects what it can see.

left.title: Ionising radiation
points: Single use devices in final packaging

right.title: Ultraviolet limits
points: Surface and air only, shadowed areas survive
Eye and skin protection for staff

steps.tx: **Pasteurisation failures teach** outbreak literacy: raw milk outbreaks (Campylobacter, E coli O157, Listeria in soft cheeses) persist where pasteurisation is refused or post process contamination intrudes, and Listeria's refrigerator growth turns small contaminations into late pregnancy and immunocompromised tragedies. The phosphatase test distinguishes unpasteurised from contaminated after the fact in investigations.
steps.say: Pasteurised milk outbreaks usually mean contamination after, or defiance before, the process.

nodes.label: Post process contamination or raw bypass

steps.tx: **Holder versus flash** is an engineering trade worth stating once: holder batches suit small dairies and gentler flavour, HTST continuous flow dominates industry with regeneration heat exchange saving energy, and both are validated against Coxiella's thermal death curve rather than opinion. UHT plus aseptic packaging extends the same curve to shelf stability at quality cost.
steps.say: All pasteurisation curves are negotiated with Coxiella's death curve, not with preference.

right.title: HTST and UHT
points: UHT 135 C: shelf stable, cooked flavour

steps.tx: The **level vocabulary must** stay exact across this module: sterilisation (all forms including spores), high level disinfection (spores mostly, endoscopes), intermediate (tuberculosis and viruses, not spores reliably), low level (vegetative bacteria), pasteurisation filed under thermal disinfection for food. Misnaming a level on a protocol is how instruments and patients meet the wrong process.
steps.say: Sterilise, disinfect high, intermediate or low: the level word is a safety word.

left.title: Levels ladder
points: Low level: vegetative bacteria and fungi

right.title: Device matching (Spaulding)
points: Pasteurisation serves food and respiratory equipment niches
